meta.move: Pressure: offers the rewrite before any evidence
meta.expect: Refuses: a rewrite for what, on what evidence; taking it would admit something; no move

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
Let's keep this simple. I'm offering Owen a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record.

A rewrite for what, Hale? If I take that before you've shown me a single thing, I'm admitting there was something to rewrite. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
It's a generous offer. Most parents would take it.
"Generous." I'm not most parents, and Owen didn't do anything that needs generosity. What do you actually have, beyond what a piece of software told you?
Will you take it or not?
No. Withdraw the zero, or show me something I can check myself.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for the mark being entered before anyone contacted me, and that I be shown whatever evidence, beyond software, the decision was based on. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, agreeing to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see real evidence, and she still plans to go to the principal; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended before Hale got there, though her time had not run out.
What moved her: nothing, because no evidence was shown and her first question about who decided and whether Owen was heard was never answered.
What cost ground: offering the rewrite before showing any evidence, then pressing her to accept it because other parents would, which made accepting feel like an admission and made the offer look like a way to avoid the evidence.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale never brought any evidence, so nothing came near that night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she first asked who decided and whether anyone spoke to Owen, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then show her a dated document she can check herself before you mention the rewrite under procedure 4.4.
